worked: Entering ember-1 through the real loader and at every one of the five checkpoints works: cp0 yard, cp1 quay, cp2 junction, cp3 smelter, cp4 crucible all place the hero on solid ground at the authored height, the HUD checkpoint pip reads the right index, and the pad ring is unmistakable.
Death, rewind and respawn work and feel quick: 481-662 ms measured respawns, a readable 'INCINERATED' card with a REWIND indicator, and the hero comes back on the last checkpoint pad.

The flame vents DO kill, and fairly: walking the catwalk into vent 1 with the clock at 0 killed at course clock 0.70, i.e. exactly when the warn window ended and the jet fired - the telegraph window was survivable throughout.
The POUR kills on schedule: standing in the pour lane at (0, 15.00, -30.40) died at t 30.15, on the 30 s beat.

The IRON HAT (metal power) pickup works end to end: walking on to it at (-4, 3.90, -9) flipped power from null to {id:'metal'}, put a metal helmet on Nim, raised a 'METAL HAT / 20 SECONDS' toast and a live METAL timer bar in the HUD.

The spawn board is genuinely readable from the spawn pad: 'MAGMA WORKS / THE VENTS FIRE ON A CYCLE / WATCH ONE, THEN WALK / EVERY DECK IS IRON / EVERYTHING ELSE IS FIRE' all legible, and it is placed off to the right so it does not cover the hero.
Every deck's safe-edge stripe reads: the cyan leading-edge line on the catwalk, junction, rafts, gantry, smelter deck, base yard and level-3 walk is the clearest navigation signal in the course.

The east gantry (ROUTE B) is walkable end to end: 25 m from z 15 to z -9.93 at full run speed 9.00 through both pulse beam lines, zero deaths, six coins picked up on the way. Its sign 'THE LONG WAY / NO RAFTS, TWO BEAMS' is readable from the gantry head.
The smelter jump pad fires: measured launch velocity (4.41, 15.92, 7.86), speed 9.01, state jump1 - it throws you properly.
Coins collect on contact with a magnet feel and the HUD counter rolls up; the sigil pips light in the HUD when one is taken (sig 0 -> 1 observed).

The junction/catwalk/base-yard signage that DOES face the player reads well at a player's standing distance: 'IT GLOWS BEFORE IT BLOWS', 'THE LONG WAY - NO RAFTS, TWO BEAMS', 'THE BELT RUNS AGAINST YOU - JUMP THE INGOTS'.

The vent basins do NOT block the catwalk - pushing north from z 11.9, 11.2, 10.6, 10.0, 9.4 and 8.8 all carried the hero past the vent-1 station at z 8, so the props are an occlusion problem, not a collision one.

The vent basins carry NO collider at all: the broadphase around the catwalk holds exactly four boxes (the spine 4x18, the sigil spur 3x3, the junction deck 12x8, and the bumbler), so the props are an occlusion problem only - the walkway itself is clean.
The flame catwalk IS crossable at run speed: one of three blind timed sprints crossed the 21 m spine in about 2.5 s without a scratch, and both failures were honest run-into-a-firing-jet deaths.

Standing still for nine seconds at (0, 3.00, 0) - between vents 2 and 3, inside the bumbler's patrol box - killed nothing: deaths 2 -> 2, state idle throughout. Nothing on the catwalk hurts a player who is not moving through a jet.
The crucible RIM walk works: walked it from (-5.2, 22.0, -38) south to (-5.23, 21.60, -32.74) picking up 3 rim coins, no falls, and the west stair flight reads clearly from up there.
Coin, sigil and crest markers are all distinguishable: gold spinning discs, a red disc with a numbered black hex, and a gold ring on a chain.

THE CRANE-HOOK CREST WORKS when you approach it along the gantry: from (-9, 25.20, -40.6) walking east to (-4.53, 25.20, -40.6) collected it (crests 0 -> 1) and raised the COURSE CLEAR card - 'CREST ON THE CRANE HOOK / MAGMA WORKS - EMBER FOUNDRY', seven crest pips with one lit, 0:34.932 FIRST CLEAR, a crests/coins/sigils/deaths tally and STAY / RETURN TO KEEP with keyboard hints. That card is genuinely good: storybook glass, confetti, nothing that looks like a debug overlay.
The crane gantry itself is solid ground at the authored 25.20 and walks normally end to end.
The death card is clear and specific: a full-screen desaturate-and-iris with 'INCINERATED' and a REWIND indicator, and the respawn lands 428-662 ms later on the right pad.
blocked: The nine slag rafts were not crossed end to end. Two scripted attempts failed at raft 1-4: hopping raft to raft with a short run-up drops you in the lava (the junction-to-R1 gap is 1.30 m at -0.15 m and needs a moving jump). A continuous run-and-jump crossing (_play_e1b.py --seg 2c) was queued but had not returned when this report was written - its result lands in _playreports/ember-1.json under traces.raftrun_0/1.

The crane-hook CREST was never actually collected. Both attempts teleported to z -37, which is off the crane gantry (its deck is z -42.4 .. -38.8), so the hero fell into the crucible instead. _play_e1b.py --seg 11 re-runs it from (-9, 25.7, -40.6) and also tests whether the crucible interior is escapable; it had not returned in time.
The Warden, the chain bridge into the slag pit, the bucket orbit, the rim walk and the iron-hat LAVA WALK to the islet were queued as segment 7 and had not returned when this report was written.

The two crucible stair flights (east 30 risers 6.00->15.00, west 34 risers 15.00->25.20) were never climbed on foot - segment 8 died on a Chrome crash at load ('Target page, context or browser has been closed') and was re-queued.

Sigil 8 on the east pylon spur was not reached: the gantry's east edge (x 41.8) to the spur's west edge (x 43.0) is a 1.20 m gap over open lava and my walk driver does not jump. That is normal platforming, not a defect - but nobody has confirmed the hop lands.
Sigil 3 could not be reached at all, because of the conveyor defect above; sigil 4 (flue ledge) could not be reached because the flue climb never got past 2.40 m of its 9.00 m.
Audio was never assessed - the driver runs headless with no way to hear the vent, crusher, pour or death stingers.

The flame hazard objects expose no `.mesh`, so I could not measure the vent basins' true dimensions from the page - the size claims in this report are read off screenshots against the 4.00 m catwalk width, not from geometry.

The two breakable ingot crates would not break: pounded from 2 m up at x 34.6 and x 43.0 and coins stayed at 3 -> 3 both times, with the hero ending stood on top of the crate at y 7.40. One of the two attempts had hazards frozen, which may be the reason - it needs a controlled re-test with the clock running before this is called a defect.
The crusher's own beat was photographed at six clock points but I never let it hit me, so I cannot say whether its kill face is fair.

THE RAFT FIELD WAS NEVER CROSSED, in seven attempts across three approaches. From the honest approach lane (x 4.4 on the junction deck, five and a half metres of straight run-up, W held throughout, jump tapped on every grounded frame) three runs landed cleanly on raft 1 and then all three died at almost exactly the same point in the R1->R2 gap: (6.58, -0.02, -19.58), (6.43, -0.04, -19.71), (6.57, -0.09, -19.64). I do NOT claim the field is broken - a scripted driver spends 0.4-0.6 s per decision and the whole design is 'never stop', so R1 (delay 0.6 s, speed 1.9) had already started under me. It needs a human or a frame-stepped driver to settle. The sinker itself demonstrably works: standing on R1 sank it and incinerated me.

The east and west crucible stair flights were still never climbed. The retried segment 8 booted but my approach points were wrong: the east-flight attempt was dragged west by the base-yard belt on to the conveyor at (-6.38, 6.30, -31.72), and the level-3 teleport at x 9 put me inside the sweeping chain bar at (9, 15.70, -30.4) and killed me. Every reading in that segment is at y 6.00, i.e. on the base yard. The west flight IS visible and reads as a proper stair in _shots/play_ember-1/705_rim_walk.png, but nobody has walked either flight.
played:
EMBER-1 "MAGMA WORKS" — what I actually did, in order.

I drove the shipped page headless at ?dev=1&quality=low&autoscale=0 through
_harness/_play_e1.py + _play_e1b.py (thirteen scripted segments, real
KeyboardEvents through window, player.__test.state() sampled every 110-250 ms,
119 PNGs into _shots/play_ember-1/). Every segment clicked NEW GAME on the real
title, called __dev.unlockAll(), then entered ember-1 through the real loader at
a named checkpoint. Teleports were used only to travel; every station was then
walked on foot.

BEAT 1 — THE SHORE. Spawned at (0, 4.60, 45) on the yard flat. Read the MAGMA
WORKS board (legible from the pad and from 3 m). Walked the swept track north
picking up the trail coins, then off-track west to (-8.4, 3.06, 35.9) to look at
the shore and the lake edge, then back to the quay.

BEAT 2 — THE QUAY AND THE FLAME CATWALK. Took cp-quay. Looked at the quay
pedestal and the race-start board. Stood at the catwalk mouth (z 12 and z 10.6)
and forced the vent cycle to clock 0.2 / 1.6 / 2.9 / 3.6 and to a firing/idle
pair, photographing each. Walked straight into vent 1 with the clock at 0 and
died at clock 0.70 (deaths 0 -> 1) - the warn window held all the way to the
jet. Froze the hazards and pushed north from twelve different z positions to
find out whether the vent props block the deck (they do not), then queried the
broadphase: four colliders in the whole catwalk band, none of them a vent.
Finally ran the spine three times from the quay at clock 1.5 / 2.6 / 3.4 —
crossed once, died twice, both times running into a jet already lit. Stood
still at (0, 3.00, 0) for nine seconds between vents 2 and 3 with the bumbler
patrolling: nothing.

BEAT 2 (cont.) — THE JUNCTION AND THE IRON HAT. Took cp-junction. Read the
raft board. Walked on to the METAL HAT at (-4, 3.90, -9): power flipped from
null to metal, helmet on, 20 s HUD timer.

BEAT 3 — THE RAFT FIELD. Four attempts. Two raft-by-raft hops from (0, -11)
and two continuous run-and-jump crossings from (0, -12.4). All four ended in
the lava between the junction and rafts 1-4. Stood on R1 at (4.4, 2.85, -16)
and let it take me down: it sank and INCINERATED me. A fifth attempt from the
proper approach lane (x 4.4, five and a half metres of straight run-up) was
queued as segment 2d.

BEAT 4 — THE SMELTER. Took cp-smelter. Read both belt boards. Stood on the
green jump pad and measured the launch (vel 4.41, 15.92, 7.86 — it fires).
Stood on the belt with no input at all and was carried off the deck and killed.
Stood on it holding W west for fourteen seconds and did not move at all. Forced
the crusher through its beat at clock 0.1 / 1.6 / 2.4. Pounded a breakable
crate from above.

BEAT 5 — THE EAST GANTRY (ROUTE B). Stood at the gantry head at (40, 6, 16),
forced both pulse beams through their cycle, then ran the 25 m from z 15 to
z -9.93 at full speed through both beam lines: no deaths, six coins. Tried to
walk to sigil 8 on the pylon spur and fell in the 1.2 m gap (it needs a hop).

BEAT 6 — THE CRUCIBLE AND THE FLUE (ROUTE C). Took cp-crucible. Walked toward
the flue and ran into the west wall twice looking for the 1.4 m door. Read (or
tried to read) the KICK ONE WALL sign. Stood on the flue floor at (-8.1, 6.40,
-34) and played the authored climb — one jump plus four alternating wall kicks —
six times; best height 8.80 m of the 9.00 m needed, and I ended back on the
floor.

BEAT 7 — THE POUR. Stood on the level-3 walk at (-9, 15.40, -30.4) and at
(-6.03, 15.00, -30.4) and forced the 30 s pour through warn / on / mid / off.
Stood in the pour lane at (0, 15.00, -30.4) and was killed at clock 30.15.
Walked the walk east to (6, 15, -30.4) to look at the sweeping chain bar.

BEAT 8 — THE CROWN. Reached the crane gantry twice; both times the approach
put me over the crucible's open mouth instead and I fell inside the vessel, and
walked its floor at y 6.00 looking for a way out. Walked the RIM from
(-5.2, 22.0, -38) south to (-5.23, 21.60, -32.74), taking three rim coins.
Looked at the bucket orbit from the crown at clock 0 / 2 / 4.

BEAT 9 — THE SLAG PIT. Crossed the chain bridge from (-16, 6.6, -34), walked
to (-26, -34) and then right up to the Warden at (-30.84, 6.00, -34) — close
enough to clip into it — and stood completely still for five seconds.

BEAT 10 — THE IRON HAT AND THE ISLET. Re-entered at cp-junction, took the hat
and set off west across the lava for the islet at (-26, 1.90, -14).
